newsitem.title: USA: N.Dakota farmers call for Canada grain import halt.
newsitem.headline: N.Dakota farmers call for Canada grain import halt.

text.p: North Dakota farmers told newly confirmed U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky at a public meeting here Wednesday that she must block Canadian grain exports to the United States.
"If you don't put a stop to this we are going to imitate the French farmers," grain producer John Spitzer from Wilton, North Dakota told an audience of more than 300 farmers.

"We are going to take manure and we are going to pile it up on the roads coming in from Canada, we are going to pile it up on railroads coming in from Canada, and we are going to stop it ourselves," he said to loud applause.
Another farmer, Jim Diepolder, of Bottineau, North Dakota, presented Barshefsky with a basketball inscribed with his concerns and the names of his children.
"The ball is in your court, don't drop the ball," he told her.

Farmers were angry about what they fear will become a flood of Canadian wheat and barley into their markets as the result of regulatory changes in Ottawa that suddenly have made U.S. markets more attractive to Canadian growers.
Barshefsky, who promised to work hard on the farmers' behalf, said she had taken the comments "very much to heart."
She said she was concerned that the U.S. should not become "a dumping ground for their (Canada's) industry overhang."
Many farmers gave a positive reception to the U.S. Trade Representative, who was described by Senator Byron Dorgan as "the first ray of hope for farmers in North Dakota."
Farmer Ron Selzler, of Kulm, North Dakota, said, "She has a better grasp of the nuts and bolts than anyone previous."
